title: Checkout redesign: decisions before the implementation plan
intro: I reviewed the current checkout and the analytics export. Before I write the implementation plan I need **five decisions**. Each one changes the scope of the plan. Everything I will assume without asking is listed at the end.

groups.title: How should the checkout be laid out?
groups.context:
Today everything sits on one long page (screenshots below). 38% of phone visitors leave at the payment section. The layout decides how much of the form we rebuild and how we measure drop-off.

If we pick wrong, we redesign again next quarter.

groups.title: Which payment provider should we integrate first?
groups.context: We can integrate only one provider before the launch date. The fees below use last quarter's volume of 18,400 orders.

mockup.caption: Pricing from the providers' public pages on 1 October.

options.label: Stripe
options.description: Best SDKs and test tooling. Slightly higher card fees at our volume.
pros: No contract, live within a week
cons: Highest blended fee at current volume

mockup.caption: Estimated fees per month by order volume.

options.label: Adyen
options.description: Lowest fees once we pass 6,000 orders a month, but needs a signed contract first.

options.label: Mollie
options.description: Simple pricing and good local methods, smaller ecosystem.
cons: Fewer SDK examples for our stack

recommendation.text: Stripe is the only option that fits the launch date without a contract.

messages.author: user
messages.body: Does Stripe support BLIK without a separate agreement?

messages.author: agent
messages.body: Yes. BLIK is available on Stripe accounts registered in Poland and needs no separate agreement. You enable it in the dashboard and it appears in the hosted payment page.

groups.title: When should the order be created?
groups.context: This decides how we handle abandoned payments and stock reservation.

mockup.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Customer
  participant S as Shop
  participant P as Provider
  C->>S: Pay
  S->>P: Create payment
  P-->>C: Confirm with bank
  P-->>S: Webhook: succeeded
  S-->>C: Order confirmation
mockup.caption: The payment flow both options share.

options.label: Before payment, as pending
options.description: Create a pending order and reserve stock, then confirm it from the webhook.

mockup.code:
flowchart LR
  A[Pay clicked] --> B[Pending order + stock reserved]
  B --> C{Webhook}
  C -->|succeeded| D[Order confirmed]
  C -->|failed or 30 min timeout| E[Order cancelled, stock released]

options.label: After payment succeeds
options.description: Create the order only from the success webhook.

recommendation.text: A pending order avoids selling the last item twice while the bank confirms.

groups.title: Which order notifications should ship at launch?
groups.context: Choose every channel we should send the order confirmation through.

options.label: Email
options.description: Already built, needs a new template.

options.label: SMS
options.description: Needs a provider and consent text in the address step.

groups.title: Which accent colour should the pay button use?
groups.context: The button colour is the only brand change in this round. Both meet 4.5:1 contrast with white text.

options.label: Keep brand teal
options.description: Matches the logo and the rest of the shop.

options.label: Switch to indigo
options.description: Stands out more from the green delivery badges.

groups.title: How should the checkout API return validation errors?
groups.context: The new steps validate on the server. The error shape is hard to change after the mobile app adopts it.

options.label: Map of field errors
options.description: One object keyed by field name. Easy to bind to the form.

options.label: RFC 9457 problem details
options.description: A standard error document with a list of invalid fields.

recommendation.text: A field map binds directly to the form and the mobile app already parses it.

groups.title: What should the confirmation page say?
groups.context: Write the headline customers see after paying. I will use it in the email subject too.

assumptions.text: Prices stay in EUR only for this release.
Guest checkout stays available; accounts remain optional.
The new checkout ships behind the `checkout_v2` flag at 10% of traffic.
